data.gender_notes: Kailashnath is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Kailashnath is another name for Lord Shiva, who resides on Mount Kailash. The name Kailashnath carries the meaning “Lord of Mount Kailash” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kailashnath usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of mount kailash and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents divine power, detachment, and meditation.
data.etymology: Kailashnath belongs to the Sanskrit, Hindi, etc. linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Mount Kailash.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kailashnath total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Mount Kailash, located in the Tibetan Autonomous Region of China, is considered a sacred site not only for Hindus but also for Buddhists, Jains, and Bons. Every year, thousands of pilgrims from various religions and ethnic backgrounds embark on the arduous journey to take a dip in the sacred waters of Lake Mansarovar or walk around Mount Kailash. This journey is said to bring salvation and absolve one of worldly sins. In Indian and Nepali culture, Kailashnath or Lord Shiva is often depicted as the deity of this sacred mountain. The name evokes a sense of spiritual journeying, devotion, and a longing for liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Kailashnath" symbolizes the ultimate abode, the mystical and the divine. According to Hindu belief, Lord Shiva represents destruction and creation, the eternal wanderer, and the destroyer of ignorance. The name "nath" is used to denote the lord or master of all beings. The term "Kailash" refers to the abode or residence of Lord Shiva. Therefore, this name implies the idea that Lord Shiva is the absolute master and the ultimate destination, the ultimate reality. The name Kailashnath embodies the divine masculine principle, the guru who guides us on our spiritual journey towards self-realization and unfathomable wisdom.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kailashnath: Lord of Kailash, the abode of Lord Shiva, symbolizing the divine and transcendent aspects of life. The name evokes a sense of spiritual connection and longing for the ultimate truth.

vedic_reference.note: Not a Vedic name, but a popular name for Lord Shiva

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Kailashnath is a name of Lord Shiva, the Hindu god of destruction. The name Kailashnath carried significant spiritual weight in that era.

trends: used as a name for Hindu temples and shrines
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Kailashnath remains relevant in modern Hindu society, representing a bridge between traditional Vedic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Hindu names.
